html:
Ukraine has formally ended a truce on striking Russian energy sites, resuming drone attacks on refineries, a move Ukrainian President Zelensky attributes to renewed Russian aggression, as Black Sea tensions escalate with multiple drone attacks on shipping. Seven crew members are missing after a drone attack left a tanker ablaze off Romania's coast, with suspected Russian drones hitting several ships in the area recently.

Russia-Ukraine: Ukraine resumed attacks on Russian oil refineries, with President Zelensky stating a pause on striking energy sites is over following fresh Russian attacks. Russia accuses Ukraine of attacking an oil refinery in Ryazan. Ukraine confirmed its Starshield access, vital for military communications and drone operations, has been restored after temporary restrictions. Washington steps up pressure on Kyiv to halt refinery strikes, with questions raised about Elon Musk’s ties with Trump. Separately, Trump's diesel deal with Russia has alarmed Ukraine and its allies, while Washington reportedly discusses easing sanctions on Moscow.

US-Iran Tensions: The Strait of Hormuz has seen a significant escalation, with two cargo ships reportedly sunk after being struck by unknown projectiles or mines, and Iran's IRGC claiming one container ship hit a mine. Iran's deputy army coordinator announced the Strait is closed and requires coordination for transit. The US military is reportedly weighing the use of the "mother of all bombs" in potential future strikes on Iran, with plans targeting energy infrastructure and nuclear facilities. US President Donald Trump stated he would make a decision on Iran "very soon," linking fresh attacks to Tehran and keeping all options open to prevent Iran from acquiring nuclear weapons. Iran's Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf said the US must be punished.

Middle East Security: Beyond Iran, the Houthi conflict with Saudi Arabia has intensified, with Houthi forces claiming a "qualitative military operation" targeting Saudi Aramco facilities in Dhahran, King Khalid International Airport, and an Aramco refinery in Riyadh. One person was wounded in Riyadh by debris from an intercepted Houthi missile, Saudi civil defense reported. The Saudi-led coalition stated 20 attacks on King Khalid airport since October 1. Houthis have issued new threats, declaring Saudi airspace unsafe except for Mecca and Medina. Elsewhere, Israel extended its rear-area emergency status until November 3 due to a high likelihood of attack, and an Intel factory explosion in Kiryat Gat killed two.

Global Economy: Global markets are experiencing an accelerating sell-off in AI-linked shares, deepened by fears over rising US inflation and AI debt, with chip makers and tech investors plunging. South Korea’s Kospi 200 index fell over 8%. Meanwhile, Social Security benefits are set for a boost to offset rising consumer prices. In Europe, an EU commissioner warned governments to curb energy prices with short-term fossil fuel subsidies to prevent people from turning to populists. The IMF forecasts a shrinking economy for Iran and warns the war-hit Middle East faces no quick return to pre-war growth.

International Developments: In Pakistan, a school roof collapse in Peshawar killed at least 33 pupils and a teacher. Istanbul experienced its heaviest rainfall in 84 years, resulting in two deaths. Brazil’s Congress approved a shorter working week, a measure Lula's supporters hope will boost his popularity ahead of a presidential run-off. Student protesters continue to rampage in Albania’s capital, Tirana, as its leader defies calls to resign. Colombia's opening of an embassy in West Jerusalem drew widespread condemnation from numerous Arab states, Palestine, and Türkiye.
